questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes the inner planets of the solar system?

options.text: They are large gas giants with many moons
They are small, rocky planets closer to the Sun
They are all located beyond the asteroid belt
They are composed mainly of hydrogen and helium

questions.explanation: The inner planets (Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars) are small, rocky planets located closer to the Sun. They are also called the terrestrial planets and have solid surfaces, in contrast to the outer gas giants.

questions.stem: According to the nebular hypothesis, what did the solar system form from?

options.text: A rotating cloud of gas and dust that collapsed under gravity
Material ejected from a black hole
The explosion of a single massive planet

questions.explanation: The nebular hypothesis states that the solar system formed from a large rotating cloud of gas and dust (a nebula) that collapsed under its own gravity. The centre formed the Sun, while the remaining material in the disc gradually clumped together to form the planets.
